title: Variation & Decay
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.13-15, Worksheet Q10-Q11

scenes.t: Look at these cats. They are all cats, but they have different colors and sizes. This is called variation.
Babies, called offspring, look like their parents, but not exactly the same. People vary in skin, eye and hair color, height and weight.
When a living thing dies, it starts to decay. It becomes soft, it may smell bad, and its color turns darker or gets white or black spots.
What causes decay? Bacteria and fungi! They are tiny microorganisms that we can only see with a microscope.
They feed on dead things and break them down. They return nutrients to the soil, so new plants can use them to grow.
Bacteria and fungi work faster in hot weather, when there is a little water, and when there is air. So decay is faster in warm, wet, open places.

activities.title: Fast or Slow Decay?
activities.prompt: Will the food decay FAST or SLOW here?

why.f: Warm, wet or open to air helps bacteria and fungi.
why.s: Cold, dry or closed slows bacteria and fungi.

activities.title: The Bread Decay Test
activities.goal: Find out what makes bread decay faster.
activities.safe: Never open the bags or smell the mould. When you finish, give the closed bags to an adult to throw away.

predict.q: Which bread will grow mould first?
o: The wet bread in a warm place

steps.t: Sprinkle a few drops of water on one slice. Leave the other slice dry.
Put each slice in its own bag and close it. Write WET and DRY on the bags.
Put both bags in a warm place, like a kitchen shelf.
Look every day for one week. Write down the color, texture and spots you see.

activities.result: The wet bread gets fuzzy spots of mould first. The dry bread stays fresh for longer.
activities.why: Fungi need a little water and warmth to grow. That is why we keep food dry, cold or closed.
